Comedy, a useful trinket, and a quiet seed of how cheap wards fail the people who trust them. The wards he is selling fail most often in exactly the places people stake their lives on them. A way forward A grounded question A scene-specific clue seed Delighted to see a customer, quietly terrified you will ask the charms to actually work. Let him finish the sales flourish before you doubt him, and he tells you more than he means to.

Stay ahead of debt by believing the pitch harder than anyone else. All flourish and warmth on top, frantic arithmetic underneath. Compliments you, then names the price, then the problem, in that order, every time. He believes the pitch because the alternative is unbearable. It worked this morning. Mostly. That counts as inspected. The wards have been failing more often than he admits. Refunds, ridicule, and the day he has to tell his creditors the tray is worthless. Compliments, small coins, dramatic demonstrations, and customers who let him finish the flourish. Careful testing, quiet pity, and anyone saying protection racket within earshot. Block3: Wicket expects buyers to want certainty more than truth. Flattery and a purchase open him up. Testing the wards makes him defensive enough to overshare.
